# Deriving the weak-source loss term from the same scalar action

Status: exploratory conditional-support; root author. This extends the
source obligation in SCALAR_SIREN_BRIDGE_v1.md. It selects no potential,
normalization or hidden initial state. Standard weak-field scalar radiation
is rederived to identify exactly where the earlier nuisance can be closed.
No compact-binary observation is treated as a weak-body experiment by fiat.

## 1. Local charge follows from minimal matter coupling for weak bodies

Retain the supplied F R/2 scalar action with physical Jordan metric g.
Let F0>0 be a nearly constant environmental value, D0=2omega(F0)+3>0.
Use F_star=F0 solely to simplify the local Einstein-frame conversion. A
weakly self-gravitating point body with constant Jordan rest mass m has

 mE(phi)=m sqrt(F0/F(phi)),
 beta=d log mE/dphi=-1/sqrt(2F0 D0),
 alpha=sqrt(2F0) beta=-1/sqrt(D0).                         (1)

The scalar charge in the canonical equation is q=beta m. Thus the charge
is not an extra chosen parameter in this weak-body limit. Finite binding
energy, screening, composition dependence or an extended body can change
its effective charge; none is removed by(1). Strong-body effective masses
mA^E(phi) instead require their own internal solution. Define
alpha_A=sqrt(2F0) d log mA^E/dphi without claiming it is known.

With GT=1/(8pi F0), canonical scalar exchange contributes
-GT alpha1 alpha2 m1m2 exp(-m_s r)/r. In the leading long-range limit
m_s r<<1, the orbital coefficient is Gc=GT(1+alpha1 alpha2). Corrections
from a finite scalar range must be retained when that limit fails.

## 2. Scalar luminosity from direct multipole expansion

Assume an isolated circular Newtonian orbit, constant effective charges,
nonrelativistic speed v=r Omega<<1 and locally negligible curvature. In the
massless wave zone the canonical retarded field has multipoles

 delta phi=-[Q+n_i dotD_i+n_i n_j ddotQ_ij/2+...]/(4pi R).

The canonical energy flux is R^2 int(d_t delta phi)^2 dOmega. Constancy
of the monopole and circular trace leaves the leading dipole and quadrupole.
The angular integrals int n_i n_j=4pi delta_ij/3 and
int n_i n_j n_k n_l=4pi(delta_ij delta_kl+delta_ik delta_jl
+delta_il delta_jk)/15 give

 P_scalar,dipole=Dddot_i Dddot_i/(12pi),
 P_scalar,quadrupole=Q'''_ij,STF Q'''_ij,STF/(120pi).        (2)

For source masses m1,m2, mu=m1m2/M and a circular relative separation r,

 D=sqrt(4pi GT) mu(alpha1-alpha2) r_vector,
 Q_ij,STF=sqrt(4pi GT) alpha_Q I_ij,
 alpha_Q=(alpha1 m2+alpha2 m1)/M.                         (3)

Combining(2)-(3) with the tensor quadrupole flux derived in the preceding
note gives the leading positive loss fraction

 eta_d=(5/96)(alpha1-alpha2)^2/v^2,
 eta_q=alpha_Q^2/6.                                      (4)

In particular, equal weak-body charges give eta_d=0 but
eta_q=1/(6D0). A vanishing dipole is not a derivation of zero scalar luminosity.
These leading terms do not include post-Newtonian corrections, scalar
monopole evolution, absorption, tidal channels or environmental injection.

## 3. The mass threshold also follows from the action, conditionally

The exact trace/scalar equations yield

 (2omega+3) box F=T+2F V_F-4V-omega_F(partial F)^2.         (5)

In a material vacuum with constant F0, equilibrium requires F0 V_F=2V,
and linearization gives

 m_s^2=2(F0 V_FF-V_F)/(2omega+3).                         (6)

A negative value is a tachyonic constant-background instability, not a
stable massive radiation threshold. Positive kinetic sign alone does not
guarantee m_s^2>=0. A material environment adds its own response to(5).
The local curvature scale R=4V/F must also be small compared with orbital
and wave scales before a flat-space multipole expansion applies.

For a mode frequency nu>m_s, the outgoing wave number is
k=sqrt(nu^2-m_s^2). The far-field expansion of the outgoing Green function
supplies k^ell for multipole order ell, and its radial energy flux supplies
nu*k. Relative to the massless multipole this is

 chi_ell(nu)=[1-m_s^2/nu^2]^((2ell+1)/2), nu>m_s;
 chi_ell=0 below threshold.                              (7)

The dipole oscillates at Omega and the quadrupole at2Omega, so(4) becomes
eta_d chi_1(Omega)+eta_q chi_2(2Omega). The long-wavelength source expansion
needs k r<<1. Conservative long-range dynamics additionally needs m_s r<<1;
otherwise the constant-Gc energy relation in the preceding note cannot be
used unchanged. This is a local, adiabatic linear massive-field calculation,
not a threshold prediction for a nonlinear screened source.

The static inverse reconstructs omega(x),W(x)=V/F, x=log(F/C), where C is
unknown. Since V_F=W+W_x and F V_FF=W_x+W_xx, a constant-field vacuum point
and its mass satisfy

 W_x=W,   m_s^2=2(W_xx-W)/(2omega+3).                     (8)

The unknown constant C cancels. This supplies a cross-domain consistency
relation without inserting an absolute scalar scale. It does not permit
evaluating the static inverse at its singular constant-F chart. One needs
the action functions and derivatives in an independently reconstructed
neighboring field interval and a valid continuation to the candidate vacuum
point. Registration with the actual radiating environment is still required.

## 4. What can now replace the nuisance term

For two weak, unscreened bodies with the common charge(1), no extra energy
channels, and the stated source/propagation limits, the previous relation is

 D_chirp/DL=[1+chi_2(2Omega)/(6D0)]/sqrt(Fs/Fo).            (9)

Here D0 and m_s can in principle come from the same reconstructed action
functions through(8); they are not arbitrary fitted loss parameters. Source
frequency is Omega=(1+z)Omega_o. The measured endpoint ratio would then
register the constants as log(Cs/Co)=log(Fs/Fo)-xs+xo.
This retires free eta only within the weak-source class and with those inputs.
It does not derive the underlying action class or certify a real source.

There is a second independent weak-field input. In the massless/long-range
limit a static weak mass gives

 g00=-1+2GT M(1+alpha^2)/r,
 gij=deltaij[1+2GT M(1-alpha^2)/r],
 gamma_PPN=(1-alpha^2)/(1+alpha^2).

Thus alpha^2=(1-gamma_PPN)/(1+gamma_PPN), and a physically applicable
same-environment measurement of gamma_PPN would bound eta_q=alpha^2/6
without a selected omega. At finite range the potential ratio contains
alpha^2 exp(-m_s r) instead; orbital force includes further radial derivatives.
Identifying potentials with force coefficients or transferring a Solar-System
bound to compact bodies would add assumptions. No such transfer is made here.

For general compact-body charges, measuring a conservative product
p=alpha1 alpha2 does not by itself determine radiation. For any positive
parameter a, alpha1=a and alpha2=p/a keep p fixed but change both the dipole
and alpha_Q. Masses and source histories being equal do not remove this
charge freedom. A body-structure equation, scalar response measurement or
additional waveform information is required; choosing alpha1=alpha2 would
just restore the assumption we are trying to derive.

## 5. Evidence and status

SCALAR_SOURCE_PLAN_v1.json freezes exact angular, conformal, mass, threshold,
inverse-coordinate and charge-degeneracy controls before execution. Synthetic
parameter cases are mathematical examples, not a fit or an empirical test.
The negative-mass control and equal-product/different-luminosity examples
are retained scientific exclusions inside their stated classes.

Primary background: Bernard, Blanchet and Trestini,
https://arxiv.org/html/2201.10924, include scalar multipoles and effective
body sensitivities. The elementary leading equations here are computed
directly; their full higher-order waveform is neither imported nor reproduced.
No novelty is claimed for weak-field multipole radiation, PPN relations or
massive-wave thresholds. This remains a support calculation, not another
milestone PR. The next physical task is the extended-body scalar response
and the actual environmental mapping, not supplying a compact-body charge.

"""Leading scalar source closure, exact and synthetic controls only."""
AUDIT_TIMEOUT_SEC=120
from pathlib import Path
import json,hashlib
import sympy as s
import numpy as np
P=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
plan=json.loads((P/'SCALAR_SOURCE_PLAN_v1.json').read_text())
assert hashlib.sha256((P/plan['source']).read_bytes()).hexdigest()==plan['source_sha256']
rows=[];details={}
def ck(name,passed,detail=None):rows.append({'name':name,'passed':bool(passed),'detail':detail})
f,fs,D,m=s.symbols('F Fstar D m',positive=True)
me=m*s.sqrt(fs/f);phif=s.sqrt(fs*D/(2*f*f));beta=s.diff(s.log(me),f)/phif
ck('weak_charge_from_conformal_mass',s.simplify(2*fs*beta**2-1/D)==0)
GT=s.symbols('GT',positive=True)
ck('scalar_exchange_normalization',s.simplify((1/s.sqrt(2*fs))**2/(4*s.pi)-1/(8*s.pi*fs))==0)

# Direct integration over a sphere and direct binary moments.
z,az=s.symbols('z az',real=True);n=s.Matrix([s.sqrt(1-z*z)*s.cos(az),s.sqrt(1-z*z)*s.sin(az),z])
def sphere(expr):return s.simplify(s.integrate(s.integrate(s.expand_trig(expr),(az,0,2*s.pi)),(z,-1,1)))
ck('dipole_sphere_integral',s.simplify(sphere(n[0]**2)-4*s.pi/3)==0)
ck('quadrupole_sphere_integral',s.simplify(sphere(n[0]**2*n[1]**2)-4*s.pi/15)==0)
mu,r,om,t,al=s.symbols('mu r Om t alpha',positive=True)
rv=s.Matrix([r*s.cos(om*t),r*s.sin(om*t),0]);Iq=mu*(rv*rv.T-s.eye(3)*r*r/3)
I3=Iq.diff(t,3).subs(t,0);q3=s.sqrt(4*s.pi*GT)*al*I3
scalar_quad=s.simplify(sphere((n.dot(q3*n)/2)**2)/(16*s.pi**2))
tensor=s.simplify(GT*sum(v*v for v in I3)/5)
ck('equal_charge_scalar_quadrupole_fraction',s.simplify(scalar_quad/tensor-al**2/6)==0)
da=s.symbols('delta_alpha',real=True)
Ddd=s.sqrt(4*s.pi*GT)*mu*da*rv.diff(t,2).subs(t,0)
scalar_dip=s.simplify(sphere(n.dot(Ddd)**2)/(16*s.pi**2))
ck('dipole_flux_fraction',s.simplify(scalar_dip/tensor-s.Rational(5,96)*da**2/(r*r*om*om))==0)
ck('dipole_zero_does_not_remove_quadrupole',scalar_dip.subs(da,0)==0 and scalar_quad!=0)
m1,m2,a1,a2=s.symbols('m1 m2 a1 a2',positive=True);M=m1+m2;mu12=m1*m2/M
charge_dip=a1*m1*m2/M-a2*m2*m1/M
charge_quad=a1*m1*(m2/M)**2+a2*m2*(m1/M)**2
ck('mass_weighted_scalar_dipole',s.simplify(charge_dip-mu12*(a1-a2))==0)
ck('mass_weighted_scalar_quadrupole',s.simplify(charge_quad-mu12*(a1*m2+a2*m1)/M)==0)

# Independent canonical-potential and Jordan-trace mass calculations.
V=s.Function('V')(f);ww=s.Function('omega')(f);DD=2*ww+3
VE=fs**2*V/f**2;phiF=s.sqrt(fs*DD/(2*f*f))
massE=s.diff(s.diff(VE,f)/phiF,f)/phiF
massJ=s.simplify(f/fs*massE)
equil={s.diff(V,f):2*V/f}
target=2*(f*s.diff(V,f,2)-s.diff(V,f))/DD
ck('canonical_and_Jordan_scalar_mass',s.simplify(massJ.subs(equil)-target.subs(equil))==0)
xx,C=s.symbols('x C',real=True);FF=C*s.exp(xx);W=s.Function('W')(xx)
v=FF*W;vF=s.diff(v,xx)/FF;vFF=s.diff(vF,xx)/FF
ck('inverse_vacuum_criterion',s.simplify(FF*vF-2*v-FF*(s.diff(W,xx)-W))==0)
ck('inverse_mass_without_normalization',s.simplify(2*(FF*vFF-vF)-2*(s.diff(W,xx,2)-W))==0)
ck('normalization_absent_from_mass',C not in s.simplify(2*(FF*vFF-vF)).free_symbols)

# The outgoing massive-field energy current, not a massless dt(phi)^2 shortcut.
psi,k,nu,amp=s.symbols('psi k nu amp',positive=True)
for ell in [1,2]:
    av=s.integrate(nu*k*amp**2*k**(2*ell)*s.sin(psi)**2,(psi,0,2*s.pi))/(2*s.pi)
    zero_mass=av.subs(k,nu)
    ck('massive_flux_power_'+str(ell),s.simplify(av/zero_mass-(k/nu)**(2*ell+1))==0)
    wrong=s.integrate(nu**2*amp**2*k**(2*ell)*s.sin(psi)**2,(psi,0,2*s.pi))/(2*s.pi)
    ck('massless_flux_shortcut_detected_'+str(ell),s.simplify(wrong/zero_mass-(k/nu)**(2*ell+1))!=0)
ck('evanescent_time_averaged_radial_flux',s.integrate(s.sin(psi)*s.cos(psi),(psi,0,2*s.pi))==0)

cfg=plan['synthetic'];threshold_rows=[];mass_rows=[];charge_rows=[]
def chi(ell,nu,mass):return 0. if nu<=mass else (1-(mass/nu)**2)**((2*ell+1)/2)
rho=cfg['endpoint_ratio']
for omega in cfg['omega_values']:
    DD=2*omega+3;alpha2=1/DD;gamma=(1-alpha2)/(1+alpha2)
    ck('weak_PPN_charge_'+str(omega),abs((1-gamma)/(1+gamma)-alpha2)<1e-12)
    for mr in cfg['scalar_mass_over_omega']:
        c1=chi(1,1.,mr);c2=chi(2,2.,mr);eta=alpha2*c2/6
        q=np.sqrt(rho)/(1+eta);recovered=(q*(1+eta))**2
        ck('weak_source_siren_closure_'+str((omega,mr)),abs(recovered-rho)<1e-12)
        ck('threshold_range_'+str((omega,mr)),0<=c1<=c2<=1)
        if 1<=mr<2:ck('dipole_closed_quadrupole_open_'+str((omega,mr)),c1==0 and c2>0)
        threshold_rows.append({'omega':omega,'mass_over_orbital_frequency':mr,'dipole_factor':c1,'quadrupole_factor':c2,'extra_flux_fraction_weak_equal_charge':eta,'rho_recovered':float(recovered)})
    for scale in cfg['field_scales']:
        for av in [-.04,.01,.1]:
            # Direct potential in physical F, with all C choices retained.
            ff=s.symbols('ff',positive=True);f0=scale*np.exp(.3);potential=ff*(.02*ff/f0+av*s.log(ff/f0)**2)
            vf=s.diff(potential,ff);vff=s.diff(vf,ff)
            eq=float((ff*vf-2*potential).subs(ff,f0));mass2=float((2*(ff*vff-vf)/DD).subs(ff,f0))
            expected=4*av/DD
            ck('physical_F_potential_mass_'+str((omega,scale,av)),abs(eq)<1e-12 and abs(mass2-expected)<1e-12)
            ck('tachyonic_boundary_'+str((omega,scale,av)),(mass2<0)==(av<0))
            mass_rows.append({'omega':omega,'C':scale,'quadratic_W_coefficient':av,'mass_squared':mass2,'stable_mass_sign':mass2>=0})

for mass_ratio in cfg['mass_ratios']:
    for pp in cfg['charge_products']:
        values=[]
        for aa in cfg['charge1_values']:
            bb=pp/aa;aq=(aa+bb*mass_ratio)/(mass_ratio+1)

# Scalar endpoint registration from waves: what the observation must supply

Status: exploratory conditional-support. Personally derived by root after the
preparation bridge; no raw GW data, empirical fit or new action is introduced.
This returns to the scalar normalization gap in BLOCK01_DERIVATION_v5.md.
Known standard-siren transport is prior art. The purpose is to test whether it
actually supplies the missing registration, rather than assume that it does.

## 1. A supplied scalar class implies a leading tensor transport law

Keep the candidate, signature(-+++), c=1,

 S=int sqrt(-g)[F R/2-omega(F)(partial F)^2/(2F)-V(F)]+S_m[g,psi].

Assume smooth F>0, 2omega+3>0 on the propagation region. F_star>0 is a
reference constant, not an inferred scale. The conformal transformation

 gE=(F/F_star)g,
 (dphi/dF)^2=F_star(2omega+3)/(2F^2),
 VE=F_star^2 V/F^2                                           (1)

gives Einstein gravity plus a canonical scalar there. Matter couples to
(F_star/F)gE; neither a physical frame change nor a measurement identification
is implied. The scalar potential and boundary solution remain unknown.

Consider weak waves about a slowly varying, on-shell background, away from
material high-frequency stresses, caustics and singular F charts. Their
frequency must dominate curvature, background-gradient and relevant mass
scales. Work through geometric-optics amplitude order only. In Einstein
variables the derivative-order scalar source in the perturbed stress is

 i A_phi [b_mu k_nu+b_nu k_mu-gE_mu_nu(b dot k)], b=dphi.      (2)

A tensor polarization e^{mu nu} obeys e^{mu nu}k_nu=0 and
e^{mu nu}gE_mu_nu=0, so its contraction with(2) vanishes. In harmonic gauge
the derivative-of-metric term in delta(box phi) also vanishes; the remaining
metric/scalar mixing involves background second derivatives and is lower
order. Thus in this specific class a propagating scalar need not be set to
zero to obtain the leading tensor transport. This statement is not valid
for arbitrary derivative-coupled scalar actions or beyond this expansion.
It also does not eliminate scalar radiation energy from the binary source.

The Einstein tensor amplitude A is the dimensionless transverse strain; the
conformal perturbation adds a trace and does not change this amplitude.
Its ray current obeys div_E(A^2 kE)=0. Let O^2=F/F_star, with the same phase
covector and kE^mu=O^-2 k^mu. The four-dimensional divergence transformation
div_E X=O^-4 div_g(O^4 X) therefore gives

 div_g(F A^2 k)=0,
 d/dlambda log A=-[div k+d/dlambda log F]/2.                 (3)

With beam geometry separately known, propagation multiplies the amplitude
relative to geometric dilution by sqrt(F_source/F_observer). Only local
endpoint values enter at this order; an assumed homogeneous cosmological
F(t) may not replace the actual emitting/receiving environments. Equal
endpoint values cancel this effect even if F varies in the interior. This
is a conditional statement, not a derivation that screening enforces equality.

## 2. Frequency evolution does not automatically calibrate source amplitude

Derive a deliberately restricted source contract before using a distance
posterior. A circular, slowly evolving Newtonian binary has fixed masses
M=m1+m2, mu=m1*m2/M and a constant attractive orbital coupling Gc. Permit
Gc to differ from the local tensor coupling GT=1/(8pi F_source). Write

 r^3 Omega^2=Gc M,
 E=-mu(Gc M)^(2/3) Omega^(2/3)/2,
 K=GT mu(Gc M)^(2/3).                                      (4)

The leading tensor quadrupole has Iij=mu(ri rj-deltaij r^2/3).
Direct differentiation gives I'''ij I'''ij=32mu^2 r^4 Omega^6.
The linear spin-two flux GT I'''ij I'''ij/5 and transverse wave
2GT I''ij/R then give

 PT=(32/5)GT mu^2(Gc M)^(4/3) Omega^(10/3),
 H_local=4K Omega^(2/3)/R.                                  (5)

H is the intrinsic amplitude after inclination/polarization projection is
removed; a detector strain is not automatically H. These are leading source
approximations, not a derivation of strong-body sensitivities or full waveforms.
Let additional positive orbital-energy loss be PX=eta(Omega)PT, eta>=0,
with no energy injection and no unmodelled changing binding energy. Energy
balance, including PX, gives

 dotOmega=(96/5)K Omega^(11/3)(1+eta).                       (6)

Thus a local scalar channel can change the chirp even when(2) shows that
propagating scalar waves do not mix into tensor amplitudes at leading order.
Setting eta=0 would be a source assumption, not a consequence of(3).

For constant redshift z, Omega_o=Omega/(1+z), Kz=K(1+z)^(5/3),
and independently calibrated electromagnetic luminosity distance DL, the
ideal tensor quantities satisfy

 H_o=4Kz Omega_o^(2/3) sqrt(rho)/DL,
 dotOmega_o=(96/5)Kz Omega_o^(11/3)(1+eta), rho=Fs/Fo.
 D_chirp=(5/24)dotOmega_o/(H_o Omega_o^3)
        =DL(1+eta)/sqrt(rho).                              (7)

Geometric lensing/beam, photon conservation, time, inclination and detector
calibration enter this mapping. Evolution of the redshift during a chirp,
eccentricity, tides, higher-order terms, absorption, variable sensitivities
and environmental energy exchange require their own correction/bound.

The orbital coupling and unknown mass combination cancel from(7); equality
Gc=GT is not required. But the energy-loss fraction does not cancel.
For constant unknown eta, the entire leading tensor waveform is invariant
under

 Kz -> Kz/a, 1+eta -> a(1+eta), rho -> a^2 rho,              (8)

for positive a with the new eta nonnegative. Initial frequency/phase and DL
are held fixed. This is nonidentifiability in the stated leading observable
contract. It is not a proof that every transformed triple extends to a
globally consistent scalar action or that higher-order/other observations
cannot break it. No finite dataset is needed to exhibit this ambiguity.

Even a dipole-shaped term does not fix the constant ambiguity: if
eta=eta0+b(Omega/Omega_ref)^(-2/3), transformation(8) extends by b->a b.
Frequency shape can constrain b/(1+eta0); it does not alone identify eta0.
No particular scalar-charge or sensitivity law has been selected here.

## 3. A bounded observation can register relative scalar charts

If a separate argument or observation certifies eta in [eta_lo,eta_hi], and
DL/D_chirp is in [q_lo,q_hi] with all bounds positive, then

 (q_lo(1+eta_lo))^2 <=rho<=(q_hi(1+eta_hi))^2.               (9)

For eta>=0 without a finite upper bound, the lower bound rho>=q_lo^2
survives but no finite upper bound follows. These are deterministic interval
bounds, not confidence intervals. They require every error in(7), including
source/travel/readout corrections, to be in the stated intervals.

In the static inverse, Fi=Ci exp(xi). If endpoints are genuinely identified
with chart positions xs,xo, then

 log(Cs/Co)=log rho-xs+xo.                                 (10)

Equations(9)-(10) can therefore constrain overlap without choosing the
integration constants equal. Uncertain endpoint registration adds its own
interval widths. They do not fix a common absolute normalization: a common
positive rescaling of all F leaves the ratios invariant, unless a separately
calibrated source/matter response supplies the dimensional anchor.

This is a route contract, not an observed registration. We have not obtained
the needed independently calibrated quantities. A GR distance posterior has
already selected a source/propagation model and cannot be reused as a
model-independent primitive to test those same assumptions.

## 4. Finite wavelength: a controlled proxy prevents overextending(3)

The exact one-dimensional positive-coefficient wave action

 S_h=int dt dx F(x)(h_t^2-h_x^2)/2

is a propagation proxy, not a claim that arbitrary F(x) on Minkowski space
solves the coupled gravitational background equations. For a monochromatic
wave of frequency k>0, let u=sqrt(F)h and L=log F. Then

 u''+[k^2-Q(x)]u=0, Q=(sqrt F)''/sqrt F=L''/2+L'^2/4.       (11)

Assume real F>0, C2 and constant outside [0,l], so Q has compact support.
For a unit outgoing Jost solution f_+(x)=exp(ikx) on the right,

 f_+(x)=exp(ikx)+int_x^l sin(k(y-x)) Q(y)f_+(y)dy/k.        (12)

With J=int|Q|, Gronwall gives |f_+|<=exp(J/k). On the left write
f_+=A exp(ikx)+B exp(-ikx). The integral then implies

 |A-1|,|B| <=m=J exp(J/k)/(2k).                            (13)

The real-potential Wronskian gives |A|^2-|B|^2=1. Unit incidence has
t=1/A, r=B/A, hence |t-1|<=m, |r|<=min(m,1) and
|t|>=1/sqrt(1+m^2). Physical strain transmission is

 t_h=sqrt(F_left/F_right)t.                               (14)

This supplies an explicit finite-frequency deviation bound for the proxy
only if J is bounded. Endpoint values alone do not bound J. Different smooth
interiors with the same endpoints can reflect differently; global F scaling
leaves Q and t_h unchanged. The proxy is a necessary caution about neglecting
gradient scales, not a finite-wavelength error certificate for a real siren.
